newsitem.title: GERMANY: TENNIS-SAMPRAS BATTLES BACK TO REACH WORLD FINAL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SAMPRAS BATTLES BACK TO REACH WORLD FINAL.

text.p: Pete Sampras tamed big-serving Goran Ivanisevic, one of the most awkward customers on a fast court, to reach the final of the ATP world tennis championship on Saturday.
In a tight, three-set semifinal which went to two tiebreaks, Sampras came back from behind to win 6-7 7-6 7-5 in one hour 55 minutes.

But the world number one and U.S. Open champion had to use all his experience and composure to defeat the left-handed Ivanisevic who has shown superb form all week and proved that he has a great deal more to his game than a powerful serve.
"It is tough to play him. His serve is so dominating," Sampras said. "It is nerve-racking. You need a bit of luck and I got that today."

On paper this match could have simply been a boring battle of big serving on the lightning-fast indoor court. But at times there were some superb high-speed rallies with both players hitting the ball very hard.
Ivanisevic wore his hair up in a pigtail at the front which made him resemble a chicken as he strutted about the court. The Croat attacked Sampras from the front and the back of the court.

With both players firing in serves of more than 200 kph, it was almost inevitable that there would be tiebreaks. Although Ivanisevic had to pull out a trio of aces to get out of trouble in the 12th game when Sampras was 6-5 ahead, the first set soon went to a decider.
The Croat, who hit a total of 35 aces in the match compared to Sampras's 17, was then the sharper player, soon building up a 6-4 lead for his first set point.

Sampras saved the point after a long rally when both players were at the back of the court. But when Sampras double-faulted to give Ivanisevic a 7-6 lead, the Croat took his chance to clinch the set with an ace on the next point.
The second set followed a similar pattern. But this time Sampras kept his concentration, sealing the tiebreak 7-4 with a strong serve that Ivanisevic could not return.
The third set was equally close. But in the 12th game Ivanisevic seemed to lose his nerve when it really mattered -- on his own serve.
Ivanisevic double-faulted to make it 30-30. Then Sampras hit a superb cross-court forehand to set up match point and clinched victory in the next point when Ivanisevic double-faulted again.
Sampras said afterwards that the players at the tournament had sent a letter to the ATP asking them to slow down the court next year.
"It is good for my game but for the tennis it is better to slow it down," Sampras said. "Today's match was indicative that it is a little bit quick."
